description: API health: traffic, errors, latency percentiles and Node.js runtime. Start here during an incident.

panels.title: Requests/sec
panels.description: Current request throughput across all selected instances.

panels.title: Total Requests
panels.description: Total requests served in the selected time range (increase() over the window, so it reflects the picker, not process lifetime).

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Share of responses with a 4xx or 5xx status. Green <1%, amber ≥1%, red ≥5%.

panels.title: P95 Latency
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration across selected instances.

panels.title: In-Flight Requests
panels.description: Requests currently being processed. A sustained climb means saturation.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since process start (min across instances, so a single restart is visible).

panels.title: Request Rate by Method
panels.description: Throughput split by HTTP verb.

panels.title: Request Rate by Status Code
panels.description: Throughput split by status. Stacked so total traffic and the error share read at once.

panels.title: Error Rate % (4xx vs 5xx)
panels.description: Client vs server error share of total traffic. 5xx is ours; 4xx is usually the caller.

panels.title: Top Routes by Request Rate
panels.description: Busiest endpoints. Route labels are Express templates (/products/:id), so ids never fragment the series.

panels.title: Latency Percentiles (P50 / P95 / P99)
panels.description: Percentiles interpolated from the histogram buckets. P99 rising while P50 is flat means a slow minority, not a global slowdown.

panels.title: Slowest Routes (P95)
panels.description: Per-route p95. The first place to look when overall p95 moves.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(mator_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{instance=~"$instance", route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: In-Flight Requests
panels.description: Concurrency per instance. Should return to baseline; a ratchet upward indicates stuck requests.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Process CPU as a percentage of one core. 100% = one core saturated; Node is single-threaded for JS, so sustained ~100% means CPU-bound.

panels.title: Memory (RSS & External)
panels.description: Resident set size — the number to watch for a container OOM kill.

panels.title: Heap Usage
panels.description: V8 heap used vs total. Used approaching total with rising GC is the classic leak signature.

panels.title: Event Loop Lag
panels.description: How long a callback waits before running. Sustained p99 above ~100ms means the loop is blocked and every request is queueing behind it.

panels.title: Garbage Collection Rate
panels.description: GC time per second by collection kind. A rising "major" line alongside heap growth confirms memory pressure.

panels.title: Active Handles
panels.description: Open handles (sockets, timers). Unbounded growth indicates a leak.

panels.title: Active Requests
panels.description: Pending libuv requests (fs/dns/etc).

panels.title: Heap Utilisation
panels.description: Heap used as a share of heap total.

panels.title: Instances Up
panels.description: Number of backend processes currently reporting metrics.
